subject: math

objective.text: Draw chips to subtract with up to two unbundlings. Check with addition.

explanations.title: Unbundle a ten
explanations.text: In 584 minus 147, 4 ones cannot lose 7. Change 1 ten for 10 ones. Now 14 ones minus 7 ones.

explanations.title: Unbundle a hundred
explanations.text: In 637 minus 253, 3 tens cannot lose 5. Change 1 hundred for 10 tens. Now 13 tens minus 5 tens.

explanations.title: Check with addition
explanations.text: Add the answer and the part you took away. You should get the whole again.

explanations.title: Use the nearest ten
explanations.text: To find 16 minus 9, use 10 minus 9 and 1 plus 6.

source_ref.section: Fluency: Using the Nearest Ten to Subtract

examples.title: 584 minus 147
examples.text: Change 1 ten for 10 ones. 14 minus 7 is 7 ones. 7 tens minus 4 tens is 3 tens. 5 hundreds minus 1 hundred is 4. The answer is 437.

examples.title: 637 minus 253
examples.text: Change 1 hundred for 10 tens. 7 minus 3 is 4 ones. 13 tens minus 5 tens is 8 tens. 5 hundreds minus 2 hundreds is 3. The answer is 384.

hints.text: Line up the ones, tens and hundreds.
Start with the ones. Do you have enough to take away?
Change 1 ten for 10 ones, or 1 hundred for 10 tens.
Add the answer to the part you took away. Do you get the whole?
Make a number bond. The parts add up to the whole.
Think of the ten you can make.
Break the second number to make ten first.
Count on or count back. Use your fingers or a number line.
Read the story again. What do you know? What do you need to find?
Draw a tape diagram. Label what you know.
Decide: do you add or take away? Then solve.
